inputs.sbc_source: not applicable to this model -- see notes
inputs.share_count_basis: diluted weighted-average shares, Q2 FY2026 10-Q (period ended 2026-03-31); NOT held flat -- Atmos funds its ~$4.2B/yr rate-base capex program substantially with continuous equity issuance (ATM program), targeting a ~60% equity capitalization ratio. This is genuine non-SBC dilution, modelled implicitly through the payout-ratio/EPS-growth algorithm rather than an explicit share count path, because the flow being capitalized (dividends per share on the guided EPS path) is already stated on a per-share, post-dilution basis by management's own guidance.
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2026-03-31 (Q2 FY2026 10-Q; latest balance sheet extracted -- Q3 FY2026 10-Q results are cited qualitatively in the Analysis JSON from the August 2026 earnings release but were not yet in the XBRL-parsed core_metrics table at build time)
inputs.units: millions (balance sheet items); EPS/DPS in whole USD per share
inputs.wacc_rationale: NOT a WACC-discounted owner-FCF model. Atmos is a fully regulated natural-gas distribution/transmission utility (Analysis JSON) whose reported OCF is deliberately and structurally exhausted (and exceeded) by a ~$4.2B/yr rate-base capex program funded by continuous debt AND equity issuance -- FY2025 OCF of $2,049M against guided FY2026 capex of ~$4,200M, with total debt more than tripling since FY2018 and shares outstanding up ~53% over the same period via ATM equity raises. 'Free cash flow' in this business is a capex-timing artifact, not a signal, exactly the pattern the dcf-methods skill flags for REITs/banks/land subdividers: the owner-FCF engine's SBC/capex/working-capital machinery does not fit a company whose entire growth algorithm is 'invest more in rate base, earn allowed ROE on it, finance the gap externally.' Instead this model discounts the flow that actually accrues to equity holders post-financing-cost -- dividends per share on the company's own guided EPS growth path -- at the COST OF EQUITY, and never subtracts net debt again (interest expense is already inside the EPS/dividend flow, exactly as for the AFFO/residual-income/BVPS-compounding families in .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md). Cost of equity built bottom-up: 10-year UST ~5.0-5.2% as of 2026-09-25 (Yahoo ^TNX) + a utility equity spread of ~2.0pp base case (low-beta ~0.55-0.65 regulated gas LDC; CAPM cross-check: rf 5.0% + beta 0.6 x broad ERP ~7.5% implies ~9.5% unlevered-style, moderated down for the bond-proxy, AA-adjacent-credit, highly regulated cash-flow character investors actually price ATO on -- 7.0% base is consistent with where utility dividend yields + guided growth trade today). Bull case lowers CoE to 6.0% (rate relief / spread compression); bear case raises it to 8.5% (rates stay higher-for-longer, funding costs and dilution cost rise, as flagged as a financial risk in the Analysis JSON).
inputs.lease_treatment: not material -- regulated utility, no meaningful operating lease footprint relative to rate base; not modelled
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: dcf-methods/SKILL.md has no dedicated routing row for a regulated utility. Per the agent instructions' own steer ('rate-base / regulated-return company... valued via regulated rate-base growth + allowed ROE, or a dividend-discount/FCFE approach') and the skill's general principle ('capitalize [a post-financing flow] at the cost of equity and never subtract net debt afterwards'), this is built as a Dividend Discount Model on the company's own guided EPS growth algorithm (6-8% long-term EPS CAGR off FY2026 guidance of $8.40-$8.50, per Analysis JSON), with a payout ratio path anchored to the current $4.00 annualized dividend (47.3% of FY2026 guidance midpoint), discounted at cost of equity, terminal value = MIN(Gordon-on-dividends, exit-P/E x terminal EPS), floored implicitly by the P/E cap. This is the standard institutional approach to valuing a regulated-return utility and is structurally the same family as the BVPS-compounding / residual-income / AFFO-capitalization rows already in the skill: discount the post-financing per-share flow at cost of equity, terminal value via a per-share multiple, net debt NOT subtracted a second time (it is already embedded in EPS via interest expense on the utility's own debt). No prior DCF exists for ATO (fresh build) and no memory entry exists; this is the first valuation, so the model choice itself is the judgment being recorded for any future update. Historical EPS CAGRs (3yr 10.0%, 5yr 8.8%) run above the 6-8% guided algorithm -- the base case decelerates toward the low end of guidance (7.5% tapering to 5.0%) rather than extrapolating the recent above-guidance run, which itself was flattered by outsized rate-case catch-up (~$334M of annualized regulatory increases pursued in FY2026 alone) that will not repeat indefinitely at that pace. Shareholders' equity CAGR (12.9% 3yr / 14.8% 5yr) is NOT used as the growth anchor here -- it is inflated by ~5.2-5.5%/yr of genuine dilutive equity issuance funding the capex program, not organic per-share compounding, and would overstate the per-share growth rate if applied naively. Capex, dividend-per-share history, and rate-base/allowed-ROE detail were not present in core_metrics or kpis for this ticker (US-XBRL-only parse, no PDF extraction folder) -- FY2026 dividend and EPS guidance anchors are taken from the Analysis JSON's guidance block (sourced to the Q3 FY2026 earnings release, August 2026) rather than re-derived from the CSV.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management's own guided long-term EPS growth algorithm (6-8% off FY2026 guidance), NOT equity CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (12.9% 3yr / 14.8% 5yr) diverges sharply (>30%) from EPS CAGR (10.0% 3yr / 8.8% 5yr) and from management's guided 6-8% algorithm. This divergence is explained, not anomalous: shares outstanding grew ~5.2-5.5%/yr over the same periods via continuous ATM equity issuance funding the ~$4.2B/yr rate-base capex program, so equity (and book value in aggregate) compounds faster than EPS or dividends per share. Equity CAGR is therefore NOT used as the growth anchor in this model -- the guided per-share EPS algorithm is, because it is what actually accrues to a holder of one share. FCF CAGRs are not applicable: this is not an owner-FCF model (see inputs.wacc_rationale).

base.narrative: Long-term EPS growth decelerates from the low end of management's guided 6-8% algorithm (7.5% year 1, tapering to 5.0% by year 10) as the current elevated pace of regulatory catch-up (~$334M annualized rate increases pursued in FY2026) normalizes toward a steadier rate-base growth rate once the DFW Metroplex/East Texas pipeline projects complete. Payout ratio drifts up modestly (47% -> 50%) as capex intensity is assumed to ease slightly off its FY2026 peak later in the horizon, consistent with a maturing multi-year capital program. Cost of equity 7.0% (10Y UST ~5.0-5.2% + ~2.0pp regulated-utility equity spread).

bull.narrative: Growth sustains near the top of the guided 6-8% range throughout the horizon: DFW Metroplex population/industrial growth plus data-center-driven gas demand for power generation extends the rate-base growth runway further than currently guided, and continued expansion of formula rate mechanisms (GRIP/RRM/DARR) keeps regulatory lag low and earned-vs-allowed ROE high across the eight-state footprint. Interest rates ease modestly, compressing the utility equity risk premium (cost of equity 6.0%) and supporting a richer exit multiple (21x) as bond-proxy yields become more attractive relative to Treasuries.

bear.narrative: Higher-for-longer interest rates persist, raising both the cost of equity (8.5%) and the cost of the continuous debt/equity issuance the capex program requires, slowing net EPS accretion from new rate base. Atmos Pipeline-Texas spread compression (already flagged in Q3 FY2026 guidance as takeaway capacity enters the market faster than expected) proves more persistent than management's 'contained, modest drag' framing, structurally lowering the Pipeline & Storage segment's contribution. Rate case friction increases in one or more of the eight states (elevated safety scrutiny following the Texas Railroad Commission's citation history adds regulatory cost and slows timely recovery), pushing growth toward the bottom of -- and eventually below -- the guided range, with the payout ratio held down as retained earnings are needed more urgently to protect the ~60% equity capitalization target without further dilutive issuance at a depressed multiple.

entry_price.method: Entry price is the price at which buying today, collecting the base-case guided dividend path, and exiting in year 10 at a terminal value REBUILT AT THE 15% HURDLE (min(Gordon-on-dividends@15%, exit-P/E x terminal EPS)) earns a 15% IRR. Net debt is NOT subtracted (see wacc_rationale) -- this is a per-share equity flow, not an enterprise-value bridge.
entry_price.note: The 15%-hurdle entry price sits far below intrinsic value (~26% of base IV) rather than the roughly-half-of-IV that is typical for the owner-FCF engine on a faster-growing operating company. This is a genuine, mechanically-verified finding, not an error: ATO's current dividend yield is only ~2.5%, and ~53% of FY2026 earnings are retained to fund rate-base growth rather than distributed, so most of a holder's return at any discount rate comes from a distant terminal value. At a 7% cost of equity that retained-earnings compounding is worth a great deal (terminal value = 77% of IV); at a 15% hurdle the same terminal value shrinks by roughly 60% (Gordon on dividends at a much wider hurdle-minus-growth spread), so a 15%-IRR buyer must pay a steep discount to be compensated for waiting on compounding they are not currently being paid in cash. Self-consistency check: rebuilding the required-return table at 15% reproduces this entry price exactly (see required_return_table), and the model's own cost-of-equity row (7.0%) reproduces the base-case intrinsic value exactly.

required_return_table.note: Every row rebuilds terminal value at that row's rate (min(Gordon@r, exit-P/E cap), re-capped at r). The 7% row ties to valuation.base.intrinsic_value (177.07, the model's cost-of-equity) and the 15% row ties to entry_price.base.entry_price (45.99), confirming the table and the entry price agree.

sensitivity.note: Rows = cost of equity 5-9%, columns = terminal dividend growth 2-6%; each cell rebuilds terminal value as min(Gordon, 19x exit-P/E cap) at that row's rate, so cells flatten across columns once the exit-P/E cap binds (visible along the top-right and bottom-right of the grid) -- the cap is doing its job of preventing Gordon-growth runaway at low rate-minus-growth spreads.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight held above the house default 15% at 25%: ATO is a bond-proxy utility trading in a higher-for-longer rate environment (10Y UST ~5.0-5.2% as of valuation date, itself already elevated versus recent history) where the single largest swing factor -- cost of equity / cost of capital for the continuous debt+equity funding program -- is largely outside management's control, unlike an operating company's execution risk. Bull weight symmetrically at 25% rather than the default 35%, since the bull case requires both sustained above-current-guidance growth AND a rate-friendly tailwind (lower cost of equity) to happen together, two only loosely correlated conditions. Base at 50%, reflecting that management's own reaffirmed and recently-raised guidance, backed by a well-supported multi-year regulatory capital plan across eight states, is the single most probable path absent a rate or safety-driven shock.
probability_weighted.band_position_note: Not applicable -- this is not an SBC-adjusted owner-FCF model, so there is no house/street SBC-treatment band to position within. House and street coincide by construction; band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0/100.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Atmos Energy is valued as what it is: a fully regulated natural-gas distribution and transmission utility whose earnings and dividends grow mechanically with rate-base investment at state-authorized allowed returns, not as a free-cash-flow-generating operating company. Reported free cash flow is structurally negative-to-thin by design -- the ~$4.2B/yr capex program is deliberately funded beyond operating cash flow with continuous, largely equity-weighted external financing to protect the ~60% equity capitalization ratio regulators reward with lower allowed-ROE risk -- so an owner-FCF DCF would either produce a meaningless negative valuation or require inventing a capex-normalization assumption with no evidential anchor. Instead this model discounts the flow that actually reaches a shareholder -- dividends per share, growing off management's own guided 6-8% long-term EPS algorithm -- at the cost of equity, with a terminal value capped at a defensible exit P/E, and never re-subtracts net debt (interest expense on that debt is already embedded in the EPS being grown). At the current price of $157.21 the stock trades modestly below the probability-weighted intrinsic value of $168.60 (+7.2% upside), consistent with a well-regarded, richly-but-not-excessively valued bond-proxy utility: the market is largely already paying for the visible, regulator-supported growth algorithm, leaving limited margin of safety if rates stay higher for longer or the Pipeline & Storage spread compression already flagged in Q3 FY2026 guidance proves more persistent than management's 'contained, modest drag' characterization.
key_risks_to_valuation: Interest-rate sensitivity is the dominant swing factor: as a capital-intensive, continuously-financed regulated utility, both the cost of equity used to discount the dividend stream and the cost of the debt/equity funding the capex program move with long-term rates -- a 1pp move in cost of equity alone swings base-case value by roughly 25-30% (see sensitivity matrix)

Regulatory/rate-case execution risk across eight states: the growth algorithm assumes continued timely recovery via GRIP/RRM/DARR-style mechanisms; a materially unfavorable rate case outcome or growing regulatory lag in a major jurisdiction (especially Texas) would directly cut the EPS growth path this model is built on

Pipeline safety/reputational risk: the history of Texas Railroad Commission citations and prior fatal incidents creates tail risk of a large one-off liability, penalty, or heightened compliance cost regime that is not explicitly modelled as a separate scenario here

Continuous dilutive equity issuance is a structural feature, not a bug, of this business -- the model prices dividends per share on the assumption management keeps hitting its ~60% equity capitalization target via ATM issuance; a funding shortfall or credit-rating pressure that forced more debt-heavy financing would raise leverage risk without necessarily showing up in near-term EPS

Atmos Pipeline-Texas spread compression from new takeaway capacity, already narrowing FY2026 Pipeline & Storage guidance to the low end of its range, could prove a more durable margin headwind than management's current framing
